brief: The canvas displays a sheet of newsprint upon which dark, wet ink is slowly introduced. Over time, the ink blooms and spreads outward, forming organic, amorphous clouds. These ephemeral shapes gently bleed into the surrounding fibers, undergoing a visible color shift from deep black to soft, translucent grey. The entire display is a constant, self-contained process, tracking the passage of time through the continuous, widening diffusion of color and substance across the paper surface.

statement: This sketch simulates the slow, organic diffusion of wet ink spreading across newsprint. Using a collection of growing particles that gradually fade out, it creates amorphous cloud-like shapes that bloom outward from random starting points. The effect captures the essence of ink bleeding into paper fibers, transitioning from deep black to translucent grey as it spreads. The continuous process evolves without external input, driven purely by time and the natural expansion of each ink blob.
